goals.title: Select the relevant inventory
goals.concept: Inventory type and time context determine which infrastructure entities are comparable.
goals.narration: Select the relevant inventory and scenario interval.
goals.reasoning: The correct entity level prevents host, container, and service signals from being conflated.
goals.evidence: The inventory shows the scenario entities.

demonstration.narration: Select the ${var.inventory} inventory for “${scenario.title}”. This chooses the entity level we will compare before looking for the resource pattern behind ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: Hosts, pods, containers, and services describe different ownership levels. Comparing unlike entities can create a false outlier, so we first choose the inventory that matches ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The inventory should now list comparable scenario entities at the ${var.inventory} level. That gives us a valid population in which ${truth.finding} can stand out on the next step.

goals.title: Isolate the decisive entity and metric
goals.concept: Grouping and peer comparison reveal outliers hidden by aggregate health.
goals.narration: Filter or group entities and select the relevant metric.
goals.reasoning: The abnormal entity must be compared with healthy peers or an earlier period.
goals.evidence: The selected metric contains the scenario signal.

demonstration.narration: Select the ${var.metric} metric and compare the visible entities or periods. We expect this view to make ${truth.finding} distinguishable from healthy peers or an earlier baseline.
demonstration.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated or imbalanced entity. A peer or period comparison shows whether the resource pattern is exceptional and whether it belongs to ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The ${var.metric} chart should now contain the scenario signal: an entity or interval matching ${truth.finding}. Treat that outlier as a hypothesis until its timing is corroborated by another event.

goals.title: Correlate supporting evidence
goals.concept: Resource correlation is stronger when the timing aligns with a restart, log, or latency event.
goals.narration: Open supporting metric detail or correlated logs.
goals.reasoning: Correlation checks that the resource pattern aligns with observed impact.
goals.evidence: The supporting record contains the corroborating scenario fact.

demonstration.narration: Open the selected entity’s metric detail or correlated logs while preserving its time context. We are looking for a restart, warning, latency event, or other record that occurs alongside ${truth.finding}.
demonstration.reasoning: A resource spike alone does not prove customer impact or causation. Matching its entity and timing to a second observable signal tests whether the ${var.metric} pattern really relates to ${truth.scope}.
demonstration.evidence: The supporting record should align with the outlier’s entity and time. That independent correlation turns the metric pattern into evidence for the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}
